critical_changes: Describe the alignment ratio beta/sqrt(Q) accurately (Sec. 4.3, Tables 4-5 captions, Sec. 5.3, abstract). It is invariant only to one global rescaling. It is lowered by off-pattern differences and by scene-to-scene variation (Q = B/H + V_scene), so 'direction regardless of size' is inaccurate. Also report the scene-averaged cosine beta/sqrt(B/H); by the reviewer's computation GPT Image 2 remains highest in all three representations (0.70, 0.71, 0.78).

Correct the explanation of recognition (Sec. 5.4 and intro bullet 4). Nearest-prototype recognition does not reward direction 'whatever their size': it depends on the size of the differences relative to image-level spread and on shared offsets, as the paper's own Appendix F/Table 26 shows (up to +26.8 points from a name-independent translation). Present the n=6 Spearman correlations as descriptive co-variation; recognition correlates nearly as well with beta itself (about 0.77 CLIP, 0.71 CSD).

Qualify the introduction's D > 1 verdicts (GPT Image 1, Flare, Sunburst in the features; Sunburst in CLIP) as unadjusted and conditional on independent repeats. Note that GPT Image 1 fails a six-configuration Bonferroni adjustment and reverses at rho = 0.22. State in the abstract or introduction the prespecified primary outcome (2 of 15 pairwise D differences resolved in the features) and that the alignment ratio, Q and D_held were defined after the D results were known.
minor_changes: In the embeddings, report lambda (observed/faithful shared term) and the mean-embedding norms. The faithful imitator inherits the reference collection's dispersion (CSD |mu_bar| about 0.66 vs 0.85-0.91 for named-condition means), and the observed shared term exceeds the faithful one for GPT Image 2 in CSD (about 1.18x). Revise the Figure 3 caption, which attributes 'observed at or above faithful' only to H*beta/4 < H/4.

Add D_agg and V_scene for CLIP and CSD (Table 5 or 23). By the reviewer's computation, CLIP D_agg is 0.59-0.80 for all six configurations, so every CLIP D above 1 (including Sunburst's) comes from scene-to-scene variation.

Give the K-painter form of Eq. 4 (painter-specific term H*beta/K) and of the 'quarter of the painter spread' rule, and discuss how the recommendations apply to many-artist benchmarks and to unrelated painter sets.

Acknowledge, or briefly check, name-induced changes in scene content in the generated images (e.g., captioner or CLIP text probes on named vs generic images), since CLIP is content-sensitive and content-matched targets address only the reference side.

Streamline Sections 5.3-5.5, moving secondary sensitivity numbers to the appendix. Consider a summary table of headline claims with prespecified/post hoc status, interval type and dependence on the independent-repeat assumption.

Commit to depositing the 1,008 generated images (closed services may change or disappear) and add a small qualitative contact sheet (a few scenes x four names x configurations) to illustrate on- and off-pattern differences.

Wording: clarify '(less for Cezanne alone)' in intro bullet 2; narrow 'Content does not explain the difference' to the title-derived content-class check on 11 scenes; source the claim that CSD's prototype scoring uses unit-normalized prototypes (the CSD paper describes a dot product with the averaged prototype); describe Verma et al.'s top-10 similarity as a nonlinear readout outside Eq. 4's scope instead of 'the same kind of similarity'.

Related work: connect the low trace ratios (named outputs 25-88% as varied as references) to stereotyped/concentrated imitation in Deliege et al. (2025) and to Xing et al. (2026), and mention between-artist specificity readouts in concept-erasure evaluations.
Strip the KST time zone from the PDF CreationDate metadata (minor anonymity hint).
Note that percentile bootstrap intervals over 14 scenes for ratio statistics (e.g., Table 1) may undercover, or use Student/BCa intervals as elsewhere.
factual_errors: Sec. 5.4 (and intro bullet 4): 'Recognition ... [and the alignment ratio] both reward differences in the right direction, whatever their size' is technically incorrect for nearest-prototype recognition, whose accuracy depends on the size of between-name differences relative to within-condition spread and on shared offsets (as the paper's Appendix F itself demonstrates).
